scope: USPS service standards and independent federal audit, United States

sources.license: US federal government report text generally public domain; no third-party graphics or copyrighted attachments reproduced; facts summarized with attribution

observations.measure: Additional expected delivery days for certain First-Class Mail products after air-to-ground shift
observations.population: Certain First-Class Mail products affected by revised USPS standards; not all mail
observations.note: Range of 1–2 days; service standard, not measured actual delivery time.

observations.measure: Post offices more than 50 miles from regional center affected by elimination of end-of-day or afternoon collection
observations.population: USPS post offices more than 50 miles from a Regional Processing and Delivery Center
observations.note: GAO says over 24,000; lower bound, not an exact count.

observations.measure: USPS-reported reduction in air transportation expenses
observations.population: USPS air transportation expenses, fiscal year 2024
observations.note: Agency estimate reported by GAO; not net savings or total operating cost.

observations.measure: USPS-reported reduction in air transportation expenses
observations.population: USPS air transportation expenses, fiscal year 2025
observations.note: Agency estimate reported by GAO; do not sum as net fiscal benefit.

events.event: USPS revised expected delivery standards for certain First-Class Mail by one to two days
events.note: A published standards change, not proof of any particular delivery delay.

events.event: USPS eliminated end-of-day or afternoon collection at more than 24,000 distant post offices
events.note: Reported in later GAO audit; impacts differ by location.

events.event: GAO published audit finding USPS missed most lowered performance targets since FY2021 and recommended clearer improvement planning
events.note: USPS agreed with recommendation; recommendation remained open on cited GAO page. No misconduct or trust effect inferred.

causality: GAO attributes some service slowdowns to specific operational changes; no inference about individual wrongdoing or causal changes in public trust.
limitations: Different standards and actual on-time performance are not interchangeable.
GAO findings include other contributing factors; financial effects do not establish net savings.
